geo.det: The output of the pilot is a service that users can run themselves for the parcels of interest, with the output being directly provided to the user. There is thus no data access architecture involved.

geo.name: Standard encoding
geo.det: The output of the service is a csv with the required dates, linked with the parcel ids provided by the user. There is thus no data encoding involved.

geo.name: Documentation
geo.det: The output of the pilot is a service that users can run themselves for the parcels of interest. No data documentation is thus provided. The methods themselves will be published in peer-reviewed journals, to allow users to understand the service, with its benefits and shortcomings.

geo.name: Traceability
geo.det: The generated output data itself is not stored/kept by the service provider, for various reasons (e.g. privacy issues regarding locations of certain fields/crops/other information).

geo.name: Quality control
geo.det: The data itself is not subjective to quality control, given the nature of the data. The quality of the generated output, however, has been evaluated, and will continue to be so, by the different users. The aim within e-shape is to gain insights in when/where the service provides reliable results, and where/when sub-optimal results are obtained. This is inherently done by the users (both within/outside of E-shape, based on the generated outputs that are provided directly to the users.

geo.name: Preservation
geo.det: The output of the servuce is provided directly to the user, and it is not kept by the service providers. It is the responsibility of the user to have its own data preservation strategy.

geo.name: Data verification
geo.det: No archived data within this service. Input data is extracted directly from the data platforms (DIAS,…).

geo.name: Reprocessing
geo.det: As no data is kept, reprocessing is not applicable.

geo.name: Persistent identifiers
geo.det: The main identifier will be peer-reviewed publication, which have their own specific identifiers. Publications are foreseen by the end of the project.

title: EU-CAP_Support (improved efficacy of implementing CAP and its underlying principles of environmental stewardship)
full: S1P2 - EU-CAP_Support (improved efficacy of implementing CAP and its underlying principles of environmental stewardship)
showcase: S1 - Food Security and Sustainable Agriculture
abstract:
The main objective of this pilot is to support farmers towards compliance with agricultural policies and strengthen the performance of their farm. The pilot offers the agrowth platform, which is a suite of smart farming services enabled by artificial intelligence, earth observations and numerical weather predictions. Crop phenology and crop yield estimation, the two core services of agrowth, constitute key information for agricultural management and thereby actionable knowledge for the farmer, the agricultural consultant, the insurance company and the policy maker. Using agrowth we can i) reduce the cultivation costs, ii) increase productivity and iii) protect the yield from adverse weather events. All this work is of great significance towards achieving zero hunger, as we help to make more with less. 

The concept was transformed to a first proof of concept (PoC) by NOA in collaboration with NP as the first co-designer/user. Subsequently, this PoC was communicated to a broader pool of potential users and newcomers co-designers/users provided new requirements/needs/ideas. Thus, an alpha version of agrowth platform was developed (satisfying also some new needs), released and tested in the cotton cultivation period of 2021. A continuous development driven by users’ feedback and needs, targets to a beta version of agrowth platform with evaluated, updated and robust versions of existing and new services. 


Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

title: Agro-industry (increased resource use-efficiency of agroindustry)
full: S1P4 - Agro-industry (increased resource use-efficiency of agroindustry)
showcase: S1 - Food Security and Sustainable Agriculture
abstract:
Providing services able to support agriculture activities to resist and adapt to climate change and at the same time ensuring the increase of productivity in a sustainable manner.
Showcasing that Copernicus data sets combined with the necessary in-situ data (collected based on information collected from farm machines, industry experts and field sensors), weather and soil data can deliver improved information for-and deliver economic value to European agricultural industry and farmers.
The concept is built upon a smart combination of in situ, weather and EO data. Data collected in the GEOGLAM pilot of the Agricultural showcase will be adapted to address the needs of the agro industry.

Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

geo.det: The output of the pilot is a service that is available in WIG, with the output being directly provided to the user. There is thus no data access architecture involved.

geo.name: Standard encoding
geo.det: The output of the pilot is a service that is available in WIG, with the output being directly provided to the user. There is thus no data encoding involved.

geo.name: Documentation
geo.det: The output of the pilot is a service that is available in WIG, with the output being directly provided to the user. No data documentation is thus provided. The underlying method itself is discussed with the end-user, at a basic level.

geo.name: Traceability
geo.det: The output of the pilot is directly provided to the user in a dashboard, not as a separate data source. Data tracebility is thus not relevant

geo.name: Quality control
geo.det: The data itself is not subjective to quality control, given the nature of the data. The quality of the generated output, however, has been evaluated, and will continue to be so, by the different users. The aim within e-shape is to gain insights in when/where the service provides reliable results, and where/when sub-optimal results are obtained. This is inherently done by the users.

geo.name: Preservation
geo.det: The output of the servuce is provided directly to the user, and is run on a daily basis during the relevant time period (May/June). The data itself is not stored afterwards.

geo.name: Data verification
geo.det: No archived data within this service. Input data is extracted directly from other data platforms (Terrascope).

geo.name: Reprocessing
geo.det: The data is, by its very nature, reprocessed on a daily basis, as it provides the optimal  harvest time based on the current condition of the crop. No versioning is done, as only the latest (current) output is relevant.

geo.name: Persistent identifiers
geo.det: The main identifier will be the WIG-platform itself. No scientific publications are foreseen, and references to the used services must be done to the WIG platform.

title: Linking EO and Farm IoT for Automated Decision Support
full: S1P5 - Linking EO and Farm IoT for Automated Decision Support
showcase: S1 - Food Security and Sustainable Agriculture
abstract:
Integrating free and open data, especially the Earth observing Copernicus Sentinels, into the decision support system (DSS) of growers around the world to improve daily decision making is vital to improving and sustaining vineyards and orchards as well as other fruit production. Depending on the regional climatology, different water regimes and plant specific information is needed to adequately support daily operations and the dense temporal Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 image coverage can significantly improve information access and content.

Climate change is affecting local production of agricultural commodities. Fruits, including grapes produced in vineyards and other fruits that are grown in orchards can be significantly affected by a number of climatic and environmental changes which reduces productivity and potentially affects the entire harvest. By linking EO data with ground measurements from Internet of Things (IoT) devices providing in-situ field measures, automated farm management systems can provide farmers and growers with actionable and timely information to improve their productivity and farming solution sustainability.

Acknowledgment

title: Service for SDG 2.4.1 and 15.3.1 indicators
full: S1P6 - Service for SDG 2.4.1 and 15.3.1 indicators
showcase: S1 - Food Security and Sustainable Agriculture
abstract:
The project provides informational service on the SDG indicators 2.4.1 “Proportion of agricultural area under productive and sustainable agriculture” and 15.3.1 “Proportion of land that is degraded over total land area” based on the 10 m. agricultural land productivity and crop type mapping on Sentinel-2 data as well as Sen-4-CAP. This project created by Space Research Institute NASU-SSAU – the main scientific research organization on the remote sensing field in Ukraine, ERA-Planet programme member and Copernicus Academy member. The methodology for this pilot was developed within the ERA-Planet programme GEOEssential project. The workflows for data processing, crop type mapping and SDGs indicators assessment was developed and tested within Amazon GEO-Grant using Amazon computational resources. The project is compliant with European initiatives on the SDGs and Sendai Framework and the unique feature of the project is usage of moderate resolution Sentinel-1,2 and Landsat-8 mission images for land degradation assessment on the country and field levels. In addition, the project aims on the extent of the European technologies such as SEN-4-Cap, CREODIAS, GEOEsential workflows for territory of Ukraine and neighboring countries.

The pilot will be implemented for Ukraine and 1 European country on the CREODIAS cloud platform. The main functions of the service will be assessment of the SDG indicators on the country level, regional land productivity assessment, crop maps analysis, agriculture statistics delivery, national SDG report preparation and field level land productivity calculation. The results of the project will valuable for scientific and private-business organizations as well as for academicals sector. Within the Copernicus Academy, Space Research Institute, based on the project results, will prepare training on remote sensing data analysis and MsSci course for Kyiv Academic University on Remote Sensing Data Science.

Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

title: DynaCrop - unlocking EO intelligence across the food value chain
showcase: S1 - Food Security and Sustainable Agriculture
abstract:
The food production sector must undergo a major change in order to sustain food production for a growing population and turn sustainable and carbon-neutral at the same time. Earth Observation is bringing tools that support the transition, but their adoption is slow due to the high complexity of the issue.

DynaCrop is a white-label ecosystem enabling companies in the food value chain to use advanced information, statistics and intelligence based on Earth Observation. It provides ready-made crop monitoring, field statistics, application maps and soil moisture assessment on a global scale.

DynaCrop pursues a synergy with companies already established in the food value chain and helps them to integrate EO-based information at scale. In this way, it minimizes resources needed for EO integration (money, time, human resources) and provides users with state-of-the-art service. Information is delivered through the value-added platform (API, white label web application, QGIS plugin) and users are receiving user-centric consulting and R&D cooperation as part of the cooperation.

title: EO-based surveillance of Mercury pollution (Minamata Convention)
full: S2P1 - EO-based surveillance of Mercury pollution (Minamata Convention)
abstract:
Mercury is a pollutant of global concern. Released to the atmosphere from several anthropogenic and natural sources, it deposits to oceans and terrestrial ecosystems affecting the food chain and ultimately human health. Its effects potentially impact on both human health and the environment, so it is necessary to take into consideration the pathways of exposure for people, and to implement a surveillance for the protection of human beings and of the environment.

Efforts at European level have been aimed to develop a Transnational Environmental Observation System in Support of European & International Policies through the Integration of real-time monitoring data from various platforms, modelling tools and an advanced global cyber-infrastructure for data sharing and interoperability. EC has also been supporting the activity of the Expert Group on Effectiveness Evaluation of the Minamata Convention, for which the Showcase Coordinator has been nominated as European Representative.

snaps.title: e-shape pilot S2-P1 - EO-based surveillance of Mercury pollution
snaps.abstract:
Mercury is a pollutant of global concern. Released to the atmosphere from several anthropogenic and natural sources, it deposits to oceans and terrestrial ecosystems affecting the food chain and ultimately human health. Its effects potentially impact on both human health and the environment, so it is necessary to take into consideration the pathways of exposure for people, and to implement a surveillance for the protection of human beings and of the environment.

Efforts at European level have been aimed to develop a Transnational Environmental Observation System in Support of European & International Policies through the Integration of real-time monitoring data from various platforms, modelling tools and an advanced global cyber-infrastructure for data sharing and interoperability. EC has also been supporting the activity of the Expert Group on Effectiveness Evaluation of the Minamata Convention, for which the Showcase Coordinator has been nominated as European Representative.


Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

title: EO-based surveillance of POPs pollution (Stockholm Convention)
full: S2P2 - EO-based surveillance of POPs pollution (Stockholm Convention)
abstract:
The Global Monitoring Plan (GMP) of the Stockholm Convention (SC) was established as an effective and sustainable global system to collect comparable, harmonized and reliable information on POP levels in core media (air, human tissues (breast milk/blood), and water) supporting the effectiveness evaluation of the Stockholm Convention. However, systems for electronic data management, harmonization, analysis and visualization adaptable to ever increasing scope of the convention were not available. Our pilot S2P2 allows partners, data providers, policy makers and international organizations to expand our knowledge, improve decision making and broaden use of data in risk assessment and their visibility.


Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

geo.name: Discovery metadata
geo.det: Metadata are described using ISO 19115:2003 standard. Discoverability is ensured by data catalogue (data.recetox.muni.cz). Data are published in multiple ways: 1. publicly available web portal (http://visualization.pops-gmp.org/2014/) with data visualization tools; 2. in CSV format; 3. in WFS (Web Feature Service) format which is a OGC standard for geospatial information. All data sources are linked from data cataloague.
geo.exc: Data from GMP2 (up to 2014) data collection campaign are available right now. Data collected within GMP3 (up to 2020) are currently under process of revision by Regional Organisation Groups of Stockholm Convention and will be published during May/June 2021

geo.name: Online access
geo.det: Data are publishled using: 1. HTML (web portal with data visualization tools: http://visualization.pops-gmp.org/2014/), 2. CSV for direct download (http://visualization.pops-gmp.org/2014/tabular-reporting/export-all/8e5c75dac947bbafa17ee8aefa887138); 3. WFS (Web Feature Service): https://geoserver.recetox.muni.cz/geoserver/ows?service=wfs&version=2.0.0&request=GetCapabilities
geo.exc: Data from GMP2 (up to 2014) data collection campaign are available right now. Data collected within GMP3 (up to 2020) are currently under process of revision by Regional Organisation Groups of Stockholm Convention and will be published during May/June 2021

geo.name: Standard encoding
geo.det: Data are available in following formats: WFS, KML, GML (https://geoserver.recetox.muni.cz/geoserver/web/wicket/bookmarkable/org.geoserver.web.demo.MapPreviewPage?2&filter=false). Vocabulary is in full compatibility with the "Guidence document" (http://www.pops.int/Portals/0/download.aspx?d=UNEP-POPS-COP.7-INF-39.English.pdf) which is a community standard in domain of POPs and Global Monitoring Plan.
geo.exc: Data from GMP2 (up to 2014) data collection campaign are available right now. Data collected within GMP3 (up to 2020) are currently under process of revision by Regional Organisation Groups of Stockholm Convention (http://www.pops.int/Implementation/GlobalMonitoringPlan/Regionalorganizationgroups/tabid/179/Default.aspx) and will be published during May/June 2021.

geo.name: Documentation
geo.det: Data are documented using ISO 19115 standard. Descriptive, Structural, and Administrative metadata are provided for each dataset.

geo.name: Traceability
geo.det: Datasets within GMP are created compiling data from various established monitoring networks. Each of them has different procedure of data acquisition and laboratory processing. Each record is tracable to its original monitoring network and data provider so the provenance information is provided.

geo.name: Quality control
geo.det: Data quality is controlled and evaluated during data acquisition at the level of individual monitoring networks. Each monitoring network has its own quality controll process. Data collected in GMP are based on data from monitoring networks. Furtheremore each Regional Organisation Group is responsible for data from its own region and does data review prior data and regional report publication. For the whole proces of GMP data collection campaign, there is a support of dedicated data manager who ensures smooth process of data collection to avoid data duplicates and other types of inconsistencies.

geo.name: Preservation
geo.det: GMP datasets are stored and operated within infrastructure of RECETOX, Masarik University. It provides long term commitment host GMP datasets and tools used to make data and matadata available. Data Seal of Approval is not currently applied.

geo.name: Data verification
geo.det:
1. Media refreshment is performed on daily basis performing periodic backups.
2. Data are archived in multiple formats - database dumps, simple CSV files with self contained description, backups of GIT repositories with wource code of related tools.
3. To avoid data loss we preserve data at 3 buildings, 2 geographic locations using 3 storage technologies (SSD, HDD, tape)
4. Systems and tools to make data available are operated in virtualised environment (single machine or cloud), HW is renewed every 3-7 years
5./6. Scheduled audits on readability and integrity of archived data are not done periodically but just randomly.
7. Primary data archive is database backup where integrity rules are applied

geo.name: Reprocessing
geo.det: Data collected during GMP data collection campaign are managed by web application call GMP DWH Data Management Console (DMC). DMC force data providers to import data in batches which comes with basic description of purpose. In case a need of any change old import batch is cancelled and new one is introduced. After any change all datasets related to GMP are reprocessed. After GMP data collection campaigh is closed, changes in original data are rare and always needs an approval by Regional Organisational Group member.

geo.name: Persistent identifiers
geo.det: Datasets are currently not assigned by persistend, unique, and resolvable identifiers.

title: EO-based pollution-health risks profiling in the urban environment (better understanding of air pollution effects on humans and the ecosystem)
full: S2P3 - EO-based pollution-health risks profiling in the urban environment (better understanding of air pollution effects on humans and the ecosystem)
abstract:
According to UN's “World Urbanization Prospects: 2018 Revision” the urban population has reached 55% and is projected to increase to 66%. Moreover, according to the latest World Health Organization (WHO, 2016) Ambient Air Pollution Global Assessment, only one person in ten lives in a city that complies with the WHO Air Quality (AQ) guidelines. In this context, open access to high quality AQ information to stakeholders in a timely and comprehensible manner to foster informed decision making is imperative. In the frame of the ‘Health Surveillance Air Quality’ Pilot (HSAQ), Earth observations for AQ (e.g. in situ monitoring stations, satellite retrievals, atmospheric numerical models, citizen observatories) are fused with population and health data towards tailored, added value products that support public air quality and health assessments, informed decision making as well as urban planning. In particular:

 - An Aggregated Risk Index for pollution impacts on health is calculated, based on satellite data, for several megacities of the UNESCO list.
 - Satellite-based observations are converted into NO2 surface concentrations to support for the first time the national AQ assessment of Finland delivered to the European Environmental Agency (EEA).
 - Health risk due to exposure to air pollutant mixture (PM2.5, PM10, NO2, O3, SO2) is assessed for Munich (at the zip postal level) and other megacities of the globe, through the exploitation of the World Settlement Footprint.
 - High resolution, population weighted PM2.5 concentration levels are assessed for the city of Bari, following the definition of the UN SDG 11.6.2.
 - Dynamic mapping of population exposure to air pollution is estimated, with emphasis on the exposure above the newly published (late 2021) WHO air quality guidelines for NO2 and PM2.5, in Athens.



Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

title: EYWA - EarlY WArning System for Mosquito-Borne Diseases
abstract:
More than 80% of the global population lives in areas at risk of at least one major Vector-Borne Disease (VBD), with more than 700.000 deaths at a global scale (WHO, 2020). Mosquitoes are the protagonists of these vectors, transmitting pathogens to living beings with the most important being the Mosquito-Borne Diseases (MBDs) in Europe, namely West Nile Fever linked to Culex mosquitoes, Malaria linked to Anopheles mosquitoes and Chikungunya, Dengue and Zika linked to Aedes mosquitoes.

There is a constantly increasing need to innovate on how the continuous threat of MBDs are confronted, treated but most of all foreseen. This gave birth to the idea of EYWA, an integrated and contemporary EarlY Warning System (EWS) for MBD, which utilizes state-of-the-art AI/ML technologies and furthermore assimilates big EO data and geo-spatial information, embodying a complete, adaptable (scalable, and replicable) and operational European EWS. EYWA offers operational and pre-operational services for MBD outbreak (TRL >7 up to 9) in five countries (France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Serbia).

Under the e-shape pilot EYWA will seek to further augment the database of entomological data from non-European territories and evolve the suite of predictive models to include non-European areas where the climate conditions are very different to those found in Europe. This will help make the model predictions even more robust in the face of different inputs. Furthermore, there will be an assessment of the combined accuracy gain of the mosquito abundance model MAMOTH with the dynamic epidemiological model MIMESIS for the West Nile virus (WNV) risk.

Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

there is a constantly increasing need to innovate on how the continuous threat of mbds are confronted, treated but most of all foreseen. this gave birth to the idea of eywa, an integrated and contemporary early warning system (ews) for mbd, which utilizes state-of-the-art ai/ml technologies and furthermore assimilates big eo data and geo-spatial information, embodying a complete, adaptable (scalable, and replicable) and operational european ews. eywa offers operational and pre-operational services for mbd outbreak (trl >7 up to 9) in five countries (france, germany, greece, italy, serbia).

under the e-shape pilot eywa will seek to further augment the database of entomological data from non-european territories and evolve the suite of predictive models to include non-european areas where the climate conditions are very different to those found in europe. this will help make the model predictions even more robust in the face of different inputs. furthermore, there will be an assessment of the combined accuracy gain of the mosquito abundance model mamoth with the dynamic epidemiological model mimesis for the west nile virus (wnv) risk.

title: High PV penetration in urban area (economic opportunities for solar energy through urban solar mapping)
full: S3P2 - High PV penetration in urban area (economic opportunities for solar energy through urban solar mapping)
abstract:
FlexiGIS stands for Flexibilization in Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and can be downloaded
from Github. It extracts, filters and categorizes geo-referenced urban energy infrastructure elements,
simulates the local electricity consumption and power generation from on-site renewable energy
resources, as well as allocates required decentralized storage in urban settings. FlexiGIS investigates
systematically different scenarios of self-consumption, it analyses the characteristics and roles of
flexibilization technologies in promoting higher autarky levels in cities. The extracted urban
infrastructure is based on OpenStreetMap data.
The FlexiGIS Module 1 is the FlexiGIS urban spatial platform and establishes an urban energy
infrastructure model. It extracts, acquires and processes urban georeferenced data extracted from
OpenStreetMap (OSM) sources.
Module 2 is the FlexiGIS temporal dimension tool. It simulates the urban energy requirement from
consumption and the local energy generation. In our case, the spatio-temporal electricity consumption
and renewable energy generation from PV and wind of the chosen study area is modelled. Combined
spatial parameters of urban geometries from Module 1 are linked to real-world applications using GIS
in this module.

Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

snaps.title: e-shape pilot S3-P2 - High photovoltaic penetration at urban scale
snaps.abstract:
Rooftop PV systems in urban areas are very interesting because they do not emit air pollutants nor GHGs during their exploitation, they produce electricity where this electricity is consumed and they add value to unused urban roofs and reduce urban heat island effect. But, due to complex shading effects in urban context (vegetation, surrounding buildings, superstructures of roofs, etc.) and local atmospheric and meteorological effects, their massive penetration in urban areas will induce a significant variability in space and in time in the energy injected in the electric grid. As far as the electric demand side is concerned, a detailed modelling of energy requirements from residential, commercial and industrial buildings with varying demand profiles for electricity is also required. 

Therefore there is a need, in urban area, for GIS-like tool for grid operators, urban planning decision makers, industries, aggregators for solar energy trading, citizen (PV self-consumption) and researchers. This GIS-tool is meant to provide an urban energy system modelling of distribution grids to plan, monitor and nowcast (i.e. and short term forecast) the spatiotemporal variability of the electric consumption on one hand and of the production of fleet of PV rooftop systems on the other hand.

Acknowledgment:
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

title: Merging offshore wind products (better assessment of offshore wind energy potential to support investment)
full: S3P3 - Merging offshore wind products (better assessment of offshore wind energy potential to support investment)
abstract:
Resource assessment offshore is an important task, undertaken prior to the siting of wind farms. In situ 10min measurements are the most accurate, the installation and maintenance of offshore meteorological masts is of high cost and their spatial distribution limited. Offshore wind atlases from space-bourne scatterometer and SAR retrieved winds are currently available online for various atmospheric heights relevant for wind energy applications. A first attempt to unify the different atlases has already been attempted. In 2018, DTU Wind Energy has a goal to develop a new, unified wind product by merging scatterometer and SAR ocean surface winds

Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

geo.name: Discovery metadata
geo.det: This will be defined in the next version of the DMP as currently is not clear where should pilot metadata be discoverable.

geo.name: Online access
geo.det: S1 retrieved winds are directly downloadable from the website as netcdf files for the actual data and png files for visualization purposes - after users are registered and logged in. Wind resource estimates will be available not for direct download but upon request.

geo.name: Standard encoding
geo.det: Output data are available as netcdf files using standard format and attributes similar to the ones of input data from the original data producers, e.g. EUMETSAT, NOAA, etc. Mapping services used to disseminate the data on the website use OGC WMS standard https://www.ogc.org/standards/wms and Tiled Web Maps (OpenStreetMap standard)

geo.name: Documentation
geo.det: Input data are available and documented by the dedicated producing centers. Final output data that can be of direct interest to users are stored as netcdf files and will be documented accordingly.

geo.name: Traceability
geo.det: Internal GitLab services, provided by DTU Wind Energy, are used for code maintainance and version tracking.

geo.name: Quality control
geo.det: Data produced by EUMETSAT and ESA are used to estimate the final products of the pilot and are already quality controlled through the agencies. The pilot products derived by the aforementioned data are filtered for appropriate flags relevant to the nature of the input data and are accompanied by sample size information. Validation excercises performed for assessing the data quality for the pilot's purposes have already been published in peer-review journals. We foresee at least 1 journal publication describing the data and services.

geo.name: Preservation
geo.det: Downloaded data from S1 and ASCAT are available online and also archived locally at DTU Wind Energy. Processed data are stored locally at DTU Wind Energy systems and back-up processes are in place.

geo.name: Data verification
geo.det: Input data and associated output data are achived locally at DTU Wind Energy using Tivoli Storage Management (TSM)

geo.name: Reprocessing
geo.det: Data from EUMETSAT are occasionally reprocessed and when they become available they will be used instead of older products. Data from ESA are directly downloaded and processed internally at DTU Wind Energy, and can be occasionally re-processed to account for imporvements in atmospheric model inputs and inter-calibration between SAR sensors. Processes are in place interbnally to perform the reprocessing and that is not something final users can directly control or are influenced by. When updated products with different validation statistics to what was previously known become available, this will be disseminated through the website and through journal publications.

geo.name: Persistent identifiers
geo.det: SAR wind retrievals performed at DTU Wind Energy will be assigned a DOI.

title: WindSight - First class input data for wind energy models
full: S3P4 - WindSight - First class input data for wind energy models
abstract:
The cost and financing of new wind energy projects on land depends on the Annual Energy Production (AEP) and how accurate it can be estimated. High quality input data for modeling the AEP is valuable for the wind energy industry prior to wind farm construction.

WindSight is a suite of novel EO-based products for characterization of the land surface roughness and topography anywhere in the world. Together with state-of-the-art flow modeling tools for wind energy planning and prospecting, WindSight can replace current procedures for land surface characterization, which are based on manual assessment, coarse global data sets, or costly airborne measurement campaigns.

Provisioning of EO based data sets for wind energy planning must be sustainable. To achieve this, end user requirements at different stages of a wind farm project cycle need to be fully understood and taken into account. Co-creation is the ideal pathway to delivering a service tailored specifically to the needs of each user type.

Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

The cost and financing of new wind energy projects on land depends on the Annual Energy Production (AEP) and how accurate it can be estimated. High quality input data for modeling the AEP is valuable for the wind energy industry prior to wind farm construction.

WindSight is a suite of novel EO-based products for characterization of the land surface roughness and topography anywhere in the world. Together with state-of-the-art flow modeling tools for wind energy planning and prospecting, WindSight can replace current procedures for land surface characterization, which are based on manual assessment, coarse global data sets, or costly airborne measurement campaigns.

Provisioning of EO based data sets for wind energy planning must be sustainable. To achieve this, end user requirements at different stages of a wind farm project cycle need to be fully understood and taken into account. Co-creation is the ideal pathway to delivering a service tailored specifically to the needs of each user type.

Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

title: mySPACE (better monitoring climate drivers in 25 protected areas)
full: S4P1 - mySPACE (better monitoring climate drivers in 25 protected areas)
org: CNR - Institute of Atmospheric pollution Research (IIA)
abstract:
In order to secure ecosystem benefits under increasingly anthropogenic pressures , knowledge-based conservation, management and restoration policies are needed. The key to that is data services that encompass effective monitoring (combined Remote sensing RS and insitu) and modelling of the trends and states of the ecosystem and its services. The H2020 ECOPOTENTIAL produced a wide-ranging set of RS variables for an ensemble of 25 Protected Areas (PAs) covering the biogeographical regions of Europe with a focus on arid, mountain, and coastal ecosystems. The selection of variables was co-designed with the PA staff on-site (narratives) that link the ecosystem state and its changes to the drivers of change and to the essential variables to be effectively monitored. MySPACE will extend the approach (workflows and procedures) to quantify current and expected changes in a larger ensemble of sites


Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

title: mySITE (data provision, visualisation tools and ecosystem status indicators)
full: S4P2 - mySITE (data provision, visualisation tools and ecosystem status indicators)
abstract:
With global environmental change and biodiversity in decline, the research community is working on developing sensitive, high-resolution indicators for efficient policy support. Over the past 30 years, satellite remote sensing (SRS) has proven to be beneficial in environmental research and monitoring (Pettorelli et al. 2014). The difficulty in quantifying e.g. biodiversity trends has prompted the GEO Biodiversity Observation Network (GEO BON) to propose a framework of Essential Biodiversity Variables (EBV). Ground-truth data on biodiversity is not only essential for providing reliable EBVs from SRS and validating them, it can also be used in a holistic manner (e.g. CEOBE proposed by Bush et al. 2017). Internationally applicable, harmonised and standardised frameworks of in-situ observations are the key to provide standardized retrievable and localised (=site-based) environmental data. We will use the European eLTER Research Infrastructure by making its biodiversity and ecosystem data available through web-based services and providing tools to integrate this data with SRS products (e.g. EBVs). LTER covers a wide range of European ecosystems (Mirtl et al. 2018) and holds long-term, localised datasets on various organisms and habitats, as well as relevant in-situ observations on ecosystem properties (e.g. primary production) and the drivers of changes in biodiversity (climate, air pollution, soil properties, land use, etc.). Focusing on the observation sites (e.g. LTER sites incl. protected areas) workflows will be defined to select relevant data and allow easier access for end users. This should include a) EO data products (e.g. Copernicus services), b) large scale EBVs (e.g. GEO-BON portal), and c) in-situ data provided by both long-term as well as ad-hoc monitoring systems.


Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

geo.name: Discovery metadata
geo.det:
DEIMS-SDR provides metadata following ISO19115/19139 implementing the eLTER community profile. INSPIRE mandatory fields are provided for the datasets. Metadata are shared using pyCSW following the OGC CSW standard as well as providing a REST-API to access all metadata content.
Metadata are provided by the site managers and data providers. Basic quality checks on the metadata completeness is conducted.
geo.exc:
For some data sources metadata are provided as EML 2.0 metadata. Inclusion of these into the eLTER MD workflows still needs to be defined.
Site metadata model is still under development based on European and international requirements. Mappings of site metadata to ISO19115/19139 is done accordingly.

geo.name: Online access
geo.det:
Data are shared using different repositories ranging from file based provision (e.g. B2SHARE) to service based provision using OGC SOS (e.g. eLTER Central Data Node). In addition locations of the long-term observation sites are shared using OGC WFS/WMS.
The location of the data files is defined in the "online distribution link" defined in the metadata. The means of data sharing is subjected to the data providers.
geo.exc: Data could be due to embargo periods and restricted use (e.g. non-commercial). Data policy is defined on the level of the data providers.

geo.name: Standard encoding
geo.det:
File based in-situ data: different encodings for data could be used based on the communities. In general the eLTER Data Specification (following ICP IM) is recommended with a basic description of the data vocabulary. Biodiversity observation data are file based following different local taxonomies provided by the data providers.
Service based in-situ data: following the OGC SOS standard
site locations: using OGC WFS/WMS providing centroid location and site identification (deims.id)
EnvThes is used as a common vocabulary to tag metadata and enhance semantic interoperability

geo.name: Documentation
geo.det: Metadata are following ISO19115/19139 including elements of EML 2.0 on method description.

geo.name: Quality control
geo.det: Data quality control procedures are subjected to the data providers and data quality control flags need to be implemented to the data as defined in the eLTER Data Specification for in-situ data. Work in the second sprint will evaluate options for quality control procedures within the mySITE pilot, if applicable.

geo.name: Preservation
geo.det: B2SHARE is used as default repository for in-situ data if no secure data repository can be provided by the data providers. This ensures safeguarding and accessibility of the data and ensuring the longivety of the data.
geo.exc: For the eLTER Central Data Node local policies ensuring data archiving and provision are applied. This is an external context to the eshape project.

geo.name: Data verification
geo.det: EcoSense platform is only caching metada in order to speed up visualisation. It is regulary renewed on a daily basis (during the night). Metadata of sites is verified using a publicly available QA tool (https://qa.deims.org/), datasets on DEIMS are validated using a dedicated, not publicly available ISO 19139 QA tool

geo.name: Reprocessing
geo.det: Data will be managed to perform corrections and updates in accordance with reviews, and to enable reprocessing as appropriate; where applicable this shall follow established and agreed procedures.

geo.name: Persistent identifiers
geo.det:
Persistent identification for long-term observation sites implemented with deims.id / DEIMS-SDR currently is not issuing PIDs/DOIs for MD records.
Persistent identification for in-situ data subjected to data providers, B2SHARE issues PID/DOI, issue to be solved for OGC SOS still needs to be solved.

difficulty in quantifying e.g. biodiversity trends has prompted the geo biodiversity observation network (geo bon) to propose a framework of essential biodiversity variables (ebv). ground-truth data on biodiversity is not only essential for providing reliable ebvs from srs and validating them, it can also be used in a holistic manner (e.g. ceobe proposed by bush et al. 2017). internationally applicable, harmonised and standardised frameworks of in-situ observations are the key to provide standardized retrievable and localised (=site-based) environmental data. we will use the european elter research infrastructure by making its biodiversity and ecosystem data available through web-based services and providing tools to integrate this data with srs products (e.g. ebvs). lter covers a wide range of european ecosystems (mirtl et al. 2018) and holds long-term, localised datasets on various organisms and habitats, as well as relevant in-situ observations on ecosystem properties (e.g. primary production) and the drivers of changes in biodiversity (climate, air pollution, soil properties, land use, etc.). focusing on the observation sites (e.g. lter sites incl. protected areas) workflows will be defined to select relevant data and allow easier access for end users. this should include a) eo data products (e.g. copernicus services), b) large scale ebvs (e.g. geo-bon portal), and c) in-situ data provided by both long-term as well as ad-hoc monitoring systems.

title: myVARIABLE (further implementation of essential biodiversity variables)
full: S4P3 - myVARIABLE (further implementation of essential biodiversity variables)
org: German Centre for Integrative Biodiversity Research (iDiv)
abstract:
Commitments for biodiversity conservation require, inter alia, the assessment of the status and trends of biodiversity. For the key users, this translates into an increased demand for relevant and easily accessible biodiversity information. In this context, GEO BON, one of the flagships of GEO, is developing the framework of the Essential Biodiversity Variables (EBVs) [1]. The EBVs are a minimum set of complementary measurements that capture major dimensions of biodiversity change, and are produced by integrating primary observations, (from e.g. in-situ monitoring or remote sensing), in space and time [2]. The production chain of EBVs often requires the use of models and ancillary data and should be documented in open and reproducible workflows [3]. The portal developed by GEO BON will deliver those EBVs to users, at various scales, and will allow on the fly calculations and visualisations of trends. The portal will provide access to the Remote Sensing enabled EBVs [4] developed within the ESA GlobDiversity and H2020 NEXTGEOSS projects.


Acknowledgment

title: Improved historical water availability and quality information service (improved assessment of water availability and quality)
full: S5P1 - Improved historical water availability and quality information service (improved assessment of water availability and quality)
abstract:
There is plethora of services on the water-relevant sectors which depend on accurate and reliable hydro-climatic information at scales from regional to global. SMHI has developed and setup the Hydrological Predictions for the Environment (HYPE) model to a number of domains to address a number of user (i.e. hydropower, water authorities, emergency response management centres, general public etc.) needs. The model runs operationally at SMHI’s servers for Sweden and the pan-European domain providing open information at different time horizons (i.e. historical records, short range and seasonal forecasts, hydro-climatic projections) to targeted users and the general public.

A recently developed global model setup allows improved water information at different geographic locations, and giving the potential at later state to regionalise the service to other regions. The global HYPE model setup is based on high resolution openly available topography, land cover and river discharge data, including delineation of both lakes and rivers, which makes it better adapted than previous setups for assimilation of EO data representing water level, water extent, evapotranspiration, snow extent and snow water equivalent. An operational application of the global HYPE model is currently in its' final development phase, and will provide on a daily basis, historical and near real-time analyses, as well as medium range and (bi-monthly) seasonal forecasts.

Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

geo.name: Discovery metadata
geo.det: Information about the data (sources, resolution, etc.) is communicated through scientific publications. The services are subject to the license Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-SA 4.0).

geo.name: Online access
geo.det: The service allows visualisation of mean values (maps) over the domain over the historical period, or visaulisation of historical data for a specific river system (time-series). Data for the entire model domain (Europe and globe) cannot be downloaded at once, yet they are provided for free for research purposes, otherwise the data are subject to commercial fee. The services are subject to the license Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-SA 4.0).

geo.name: Standard encoding
geo.det: Output data are available as txt or netcdf files using standard format and attributes. Mapping services used to disseminate the data on the website (https://hypeweb.smhi.se/explore-water/) use OGC WMS standards.

geo.name: Documentation
geo.det: All EO data providers are acknowledged in our services and publications. In addition, we provide a website with description of the models and variables https://hypeweb.smhi.se/model-water/documentation-download-open-source-code/

geo.name: Traceability
geo.det: There are scripts that allow extraction of data for regions of interest and also generation in a NetCDF format. These scripts can be improved, and are semi-automatized.

geo.name: Quality control
geo.det: There is always quality assurance of the data generated. There is a model performance assessment and this is partially presented in the website https://hypeweb.smhi.se/explore-water/model-performances/ and/or the scientific publications.

geo.name: Preservation
geo.det: Data are stored in the organisation's servers. However, if there is a newly improved model version, then new data are generated.

geo.name: Data verification
geo.det: Input and output data are archived locally at the SMHI's servers

geo.name: Reprocessing
geo.det: When a new hydrological model version is released, new historical data are generated, and also the models are re-evaluated.

geo.name: Persistent identifiers
geo.det: We make references to scientific publications that are assigned unique DOI. Currently we do not have DOI for each model version and corresponding data.

title: Satellite Earth Observation-derived water bodies and floodwater record over Europe (better estimation of flood hazard)
full: S5P2 - Satellite Earth Observation-derived water bodies and floodwater record over Europe (better estimation of flood hazard)
org: Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology
abstract:
Hydrological extremes such as floods have enormous environmental, social and economic consequences and it is expected that climate change effects combined with a growing population in ill-planned flood-prone coastal and riverine areas will increase their impacts in the future. With more lives and assets at risk, governments are increasingly investing in flood reduction measures to improve or at least maintain the current safety level. Understanding historical trends in flooding greatly enhances the ability of flood managers to take action and to address the underlying risk. The HASARD mapping algorithm that was recently implemented on the European Space Agency’s (ESA) Grid Processing On Demand (GPOD) environment enables systematic, automatic and reliable spaceborne Synthetic Aperture Radar-based (SAR) mapping of terrestrial water bodies.
The proposed pilot intends to upscale and operationalize the HASARD service so that a water bodies and floodwater record is generated at large scale and over a long period to support flooding-related disaster risk reduction In Europe. By contributing to a better understanding, monitoring and prediction of risks of extreme weather events and enabling a better resilience of our societies to such events, the pilot directly connects to the sustainable development goals 11 (Sustainable cities and communities) and 13 (Take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts).

The e-shape emonstrator has evolved into an operational service in 2022. The flood mapping pilot is now part of the global flood monitoring service of the Copernicus Emergency Management service. The different GFM products can be found here: https://global-flood.emergency.copernicus.eu/technical-information/glofas-gfm/. To access the data you will need to create a user account.

Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

geo.name: Discovery metadata
geo.det:
The eshape deliverable (i.e. a European record of Sentinel-1 derived flood extent maps) will be generated as part of the new Global Flood Mapping component of the Copernicus Emergency Managament Service. A requirement of CEMS is that API Endpoints will be developed according to RESTful standards. CEMS requires that the proposed data access and dissemination system is designed under the proposition to follow four fundamental goals in accessing the product access system. Access to the actively maintained metadata base is given via the well-defined OGC CSW standard referred to as metadata catalogue 
• easy to use and yet highly powerful access and dissemination methods, 
• high availability with state-of-the-art failover scenarios, 
• mature scale-out in terms of load to serve when needed in time and 
• fully integrable in existing solutions like the CEMS platform by applying open and flexible technology stacks.

geo.name: Online access
geo.det: Our partners from Geoville are responsible for the online access to the CEMS database. According to them the development of the dissemination system will be done in an agile software development process, to ensure high quality and delivery in time. API Endpoints will be developed according to RESTful standards. To provide an interactive access to all products a geographic render engine as a Web-Map Service will be provided. We will implement MapServer. Beyond browsing GIS data, MapServer allows to create maps.

geo.name: Standard encoding
geo.det: I need to collect more information on the data encoding standards and their applicability to our pilot's data set. I do not have much knowledge about this.

geo.name: Documentation
geo.det: A product definition document is currently in preparation. It provides a detailed presentation of the technical specifications of all project-related outputs. For each step of the processing chain the corresponding algorithms are documented in the PDD. Infomation on quality control is also provided as well as references to scientific publications

geo.name: Traceability
geo.det: Sentinel-1 GRD scenes are downloaded to EODC followed by quality checks and the ingestion of the corresponding metadata data into the operated metadata infrastructure. In the pre-processing of the Sentinel-1 GRD data takes place. Metadata records are produced and inserted into the metadata database upon completion of the pre-processing task. The third part of the workflow relates to the actual generation of the flood product. The flood product is stored in the Sentinel-1 20m flood datacube with metadata written to the metadata infrastructure.

geo.name: Quality control
geo.det: Quality Control procedures will be applied to perform in a systematic and planned manner automated and manual rigorous quality control checks considering the full processing chain, from the satellite input imagery to all generated output products.

geo.name: Preservation
geo.det: The configuration of the EODC facility hosting the pilot's data sets allows the simultaneous failure of multiple disks, and storage controllers without the risk of data loss, or interruption of the service. Furthermore, the relevant data of the pilot itself is mirrored across locations

geo.name: Data verification
geo.det: See DMP-7 for more information on data preservazion. No additional information can be provided at this stage.

geo.name: Reprocessing
geo.det: Regular data reprocessing is planned as part of the operational Global Flood Monitoring Service. We will continuously evaluate the possibility to evolve the flood production system, as several algorithmic enhancements are expected to be available for implementation in the coming years. This includes enhanced methods for flood detection, uncertainty estimation, and exclusion masking, the extended attribution of local meteorological conditions, as well as system enhancements leading to improved usability and spatio-temporal coverage, anticipating an increase in capacity and timeliness of measurements of the Sentinel-1 mission (e.g. by the addition of the Sentinel-1C sensor). A reprocessing workflow will be optimised for High Performance Computing through parallelisation and most direct interfaces to the Sentinel-1 data cube. This will allow us to perform requested reprocessing tasks of the global GFM product archive, aiming for a comprehensive, consistent, and harmonised product.

geo.name: Persistent identifiers
geo.det: A concept for defining identifiers still needs to be elaborated.

title: Diver Information on Visibility in Europe (coastal water quality monitoring)
full: S5P3 - Diver Information on Visibility in Europe (coastal water quality monitoring)
abstract:
SCUBA Diving is a popular sports activity as well as a crucial commercial service for many coastal economic areas. There are approximately 3.2 million active divers in Europe, based on data provided by Recreational Scuba Training Council (RSTC).

Visibility in the water is a safety factor in both recreational and commercial diving as well as a large factor in the enjoyment of recreational diving. Visibility can be affected by many factors or variables which can be measured from space. To enable the use of earth observation data in these user focused downstream services we will create a location based middleware web service that provides near real time (NRT) visibility information for a specific location based on EO data.

Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

geo.name: Discovery metadata
geo.det: DIVE is a simple mobile application. All interaction with the data (visibilty scores) is through the application. It would be possible to expose the data in other ways but this is out of scope at the moment. The base data that the scores are generted from is already available through CMEMS.

geo.name: Online access
geo.det: DIVE is a simple mobile application. All interaction with the data (visibilty scores) is through the application. It would be possible to expose the data in other ways but this is out of scope at the moment. The base data that the scores are generted from is already available through CMEMS.

geo.name: Standard encoding
geo.det: Data is represented as a simple unitless value (score). Communication with the mobile app uses JSON but it would be possible at a later date to expose the data through an OGC service such as WFS. This is out of scope for the current work plan.

geo.name: Documentation
geo.det: The underlying CMEMS data fulfils this criteria, however the app just provides a simple view of the visibilty scores. The internal API will be documented.

geo.name: Traceability
geo.det: We will provide documentation of the source data provenance (CMEMS) and any processing.

geo.name: Quality control
geo.det: During app development we will validate visiibilty scores against in situ data. Later versions of the app will allow the user to feedback a score which can be used to validate the data. The ratings will be made available through the app.

geo.name: Preservation
geo.det: All app data can be recreated if necessary from the original CMEMS datasets.

geo.name: Data verification
geo.det: Data can be recreated easily from CMEMS.

geo.name: Reprocessing
geo.det: This is a new data product and is aimed at general users rather than the scientific community. If as a result of improved processing we are able to increase the accuracy of our scores then we will reprocess historical data to enable trends to be visualised more clearly.

geo.name: Persistent identifiers
geo.det: Our users will not be working with the datasets but will be accessing simple scores so this is not required.

title: Sargassum detection for seasonal planning (marine algae and plastics monitoring)
full: S5P4 - Sargassum detection for seasonal planning (marine algae and plastics monitoring)
abstract:
Unprecedented massive landings of sargassum have been observed since 2011 along the shorelines of a huge area encompassing the Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean Sea. The phenomenon is highly reported in West Indies (Guadeloupe, Martinique, Barbados ...), Dominican Republic, Mexico, Costa Rica, Texas, etc. Algae arrive from the open sea as large rafts (tenths of km) after having drifted over long distances, probably from Brazil or the Gulf of Guinea.

This issue has tremendous negative impacts over local communities, marine environment and industry. In particular, the tourism and fishing sectors and drastically affected.

abstract:
Reconciling food security with the sustainable use of biotic renewable resources, including marine resources, while ensuring environmental protection is the major aim of the Bioeconomy Strategy. The current policy context in which the Bioeconomy operates is included in the agendas of the UN, embedded in the SDGs, and in the EU, demanding better monitoring and assessment frameworks. In this pilot, access to high quality monitoring data on marine ecosystems, including data on the human uses and environmental data, is determinant in driving research and promoting better advice in line with the Common fishing Policy (CFP) and the Marine Strategy Framework Directive (MSFD) objectives.

geo.name: Discovery metadata
geo.det: The service and output products corresponding will all be exposed in the NExtGEOSS catalogue and therefore will follow the service and data collection metada model which follows the ISO9115 standard

geo.name: Online access
geo.det: The metadata of all output products generated by the pilot will be exposed via the OpenSearch interface of the NextGEOSS catalogue. The metada will include the link to the different data resources. The data will also be available for visualisation and analysis via the geoportal using OGC standards for Web Mapping Services (WMS and WFS). The  NExtGEOSS catalogue is open to everyone but it does have an SSO user management solution

geo.name: Standard encoding
geo.det: Currently all products are produced in netcdf or shapefile formats (depending on the product) but the selection of these formats did not take into account any standards because we are not aware of any that apply to fisheries management  products. During Sprint 2 we will interact with the data amangement team from e-shape to understand if these standards exist and if we are able to follow them. For the metadata we followed partially the metadata vocabulary standard provided by the Fisheries Reference Metadata (http://www.fao.org/fishery/rtms/en) developed by FAO. We will continue our effort to adapt our metadata vocabulary to this standard but we cannot comit to have it fully compliant by the end of the project

geo.name: Documentation
geo.det: All products from this pilot will be integrated in NextGEOSS, following a ISO-19115 compliant metadata model defined by the NextGEOSS team

geo.name: Traceability
geo.det: Currently we have not implemented this in the metadata nor have we thought about a strategy to include provenance data into the product metadata. We hope be able to do this in Sprint 2 with the support of the data management e-shape team but it is still not clear to us if we will be able to.

geo.name: Quality control
geo.det: Curently the product metada does include a field for Data Quality with information on positional and temporal accuracy and consistency of the data. We will extend these fields to all new products to be developed in Sprint 2.

geo.name: Preservation
geo.det: Since all data from this pilot will be made in NextGEOSS, the GEO European Data Hub  we hope that this infrstructure is able to assure these requirements of long term preservation of data. Nevertheless we still need to engage with the team responsible for this to understand if we would be able to comply with this.

geo.name: Data verification
geo.det: In NextGEOSS there are mechanisms in place that will assure integrity, authenticity and readability of all produced data and all data products will take advantage of this

geo.name: Reprocessing
geo.det: All product processing chains will be fully automatic, allowing for automatic reprocessing of all data products, whenever deemed necessary by the pilot operations team. Whenever this happens ingestion of those newly generated datasets into the nextGEOSS catalogue will also be automatically done

geo.name: Persistent identifiers
geo.det: The functionality to assign persistent unique and resolvable indentifiers to all pilot data products is assured by the NextGEOSS catalogue. Nevertheless we need to engage with the responsible team in NExtGEOSS to guarantee this fucntionality

title: EO based phytoplankton biomass for WFD reporting
full: S5P6 - EO based phytoplankton biomass for WFD reporting
abstract:
A good water quality is the base of a healthy ecosystem with rich biodiversity. Aquatic ecosystems also provide essential services for drinking water, irrigation, recreation, aquaculture and fisheries. The EU Water Framework Directive recognizes this and requires member states to monitor and, if necessary, improve water quality. Although the spatial component is key to gain insight in the processes in water, regular sample-based monitoring only provides point data.

The use of earth observation (EO) data for contributing to this purpose was promoted by the H2020 EOMORES and CoastObs white paper 'Satellite-assisted monitoring of water quality to support the implementation of the Water Framework Directive'. To generate further recognition and support for EO based products in the scope of the WFD at political, administrative and management levels, WFD ecological status maps of phytoplankton biomass based on EO data are being developed, thereby adjusting to local water types and WFD threshold differences. WFD ecological status products of phytoplankton biomass are made for lake Saadjärv and lake Lauwersmeer, with a potential to roll out the approach. https://www.waterinsight.nl/projects/e-shape

Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

geo.name: Discovery metadata
geo.det: We want to make 1 year of products of the type that our pilot users require, public as demonstration for other potential users. However, depending on our pilot users' requirements, the products might be data files (e.g. geotiff) or e.g. statistics (in a plot as .png file). The first type can fulfill the requirements, the latter not. Our main objective is to make products with a high usability, so the users' requirements is the most important for defining our data production. If our users prefer data files, we will work on making them available according to the standards. We will probably be able to make the meta data available via GEOSS and link to the data via a URL to our web portal for viewing and/or via a download data package link in ZENODO/OpenAIRE.
geo.exc: See detials: Our main objective is to make products with a high usability. If the users choose for e.g. statistics in a plot and we deliver them .png files, we cannot fulfil the criteria. Also, we will make 1 year open available, the other 2 year we will keep for commercialisation

geo.name: Online access
geo.det: If our users prefer data files, we will probably make them available to them via our portal (waterinsight.lizard.net). However, users might also prefer ftp or other, in which case the preference of the user it the most important. Our portal is online and easy accessible. Downloads will provide standard formatted files (geotiff). It does not support OpenDap etc.
geo.exc: Our main objective is to make products with a high usability. If the users choose for e.g. statistics in a plot and we deliver them .png files, we cannot fulfil the criteria. Also, we will make 1 year open available, the other 2 year we will keep for commercialisation

geo.name: Standard encoding
geo.det: We will generate EO based phytoplankton biomass products according to national standards and guidelines (inplementing national or water body specific thresholds etc). However, there are no guidelines on how to deal with spatial (EO) data. In co-design with our pilot users we will define the products as they best suit them.
geo.exc: Standards for EO-based products for WFD reporting are not existing

snaps.title: e-shape pilot S5-P6 - EO based phytoplankton biomass for WFD reporting
snaps.abstract:
A good water quality is the base of a healthy ecosystem with rich biodiversity. Aquatic ecosystems also provide essential services for drinking water, irrigation, recreation, aquaculture and fisheries. The EU Water Framework Directive recognizes this and requires member states to monitor and, if necessary, improve water quality. Although the spatial component is key to gain insight in the processes in water, regular sample-based monitoring only provides point data.

The use of earth observation (EO) data for contributing to this purpose was promoted by the H2020 EOMORES and CoastObs white paper 'Satellite-assisted monitoring of water quality to support the implementation of the Water Framework Directive'. To generate further recognition and support for EO based products in the scope of the WFD at political, administrative and management levels, WFD ecological status maps of phytoplankton biomass based on EO data are being developed, thereby adjusting to local water types and WFD threshold differences. WFD ecological status products of phytoplankton biomass are made for lake Saadjärv and lake Lauwersmeer, with a potential to roll out the approach. https://www.waterinsight.nl/projects/e-shape

title: Rheticus AquaculturePlus
full: S5P7 - Rheticus AquaculturePlus
abstract:
Aquafarmers faces new challenges due to the impact of extreme events mostly related to climate change, leading to changes in the sea temperature and phytoplankton, affecting growth rates and mortality of shellfishes and, therefore, the productivity of farms and the quality of products. As a consequence, aquafarmers can’t rely totally on well-known and established farming practices. 

Using satellite data and derived measurements of water parameters and a model for shellfish growth, Planetek is delivering Rheticus® Aquaculture service, providing information to aquafarmers about mussels’ growth rates, consisting of weekly bulletins with indicators calculated by the algorithms. 

Within the e-shape project, by organizing pilots in different plants in the Mediterranean Sea with the collaboration of the aquafarmers associations, we intend to scale up the adoption of the Rheticus® Aquaculture service in the Mediterranean and worldwide markets. We will pursue it by codesigning the service with the end-users, and adapting it to the different needs that different areas will require.

Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

title: Data for Detection, Discrimination and Distribution (4D) of Volcanic ash
full: S6P1 - Data for Detection, Discrimination and Distribution (4D) of Volcanic ash
org: CNR - Istituto di Metodologie per l'Analisi Ambientale
abstract:
Volcanic eruptions are a natural disaster with great impact on society and environment. Even if they are relatively rare, the effects of eruptions on human activities and economy can be very severe. The aviation crisis in 2010, that resulted in 1.3 billion Euro damage, showcased the significant impacts to the general economic activity in Europe.

As reported in the EU Directive on European critical infrastructures and the assessment of the need to improve their protection, there is a need to improve the critical infrastructure protection capability in Europe and to help reduce vulnerabilities concerning critical infrastructures. In particular, air traffic is indicated as a European critical infrastructure.

Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

geo.det: The Pilot does not aim to develop a vizualization platform, but to use existing platforms for assuring visibility of the pilot and accommodating the user needs. At the time being, the best solution seems to be the use of the H-2020 EUNADICS-AV data portal that is interoperable with some restrictions.
geo.exc: We expect that access to metadata will have no limitation, while the direct access to the input data could have some limitations for some of the datasets used.

geo.name: Online access
geo.det: The main outcome is a visualization platform and not a data access service. Whenever part of the data will be made available, a solution such as OPeNDAP will be used.

geo.name: Standard encoding
geo.det: EO4DASH integrates data from different platforms and therefore with different standards. Nonetheless, the data are collected centrally from the different partners and converted in NetCDF format, so that these can be ingested into interoperable systems.
geo.exc: Some satellite images could be an exception. The data conversion is planned for Sprint 2.

geo.name: Documentation
geo.det: For most of the data used for the Pilot, full documentation is already available. The advanced post-processing products will be or are already documented in scientific papers. It is not clear to me what interoperability means.

geo.name: Traceability
geo.det: Provenance of the EO4DASH outcomes depends on the provenance of the original data: e.g . for ACTRIS RI data, the provenance is fully ensured and documented. However, EO4DASH is not producing data.

geo.det: EO4DASH is not producing data.

geo.name: Preservation
geo.det: EO4DASH is not producing data.

geo.det: The collection of data are related to a Demonstration Case and to data collected during a planned campaign for which such implementation is required.

geo.name: Reprocessing
geo.det: The collection of data are related to a Demonstration Case and to data collected during a planned campaign for which such implementation is required.

geo.name: Persistent identifiers
geo.det: This could be implemented with a doi assignement for the collection of data related to the Demonstration Case.

title: GEOSS for Disasters in Urban Environment (improved resilience of cities, infrastructure and ecosystems to disasters)
full: S6P2 - GEOSS for Disasters in Urban Environment (improved resilience of cities, infrastructure and ecosystems to disasters)
org: Fondazione CIMA, Centro Internazionale in Monitoraggio Ambientale
abstract:
This pilot application will exploit the new capacities for designing and delivering innovative services for extreme-scale hydro-meteorological modelling, using Copernicus data and core services directly ingested through the Copernicus Open Access Hub APIS, and the DIAS platform, as well as citizen scientists data, to enable more precise predictions and decision-making support for high impact weather events in urban and peri urban environment. Contributing to the Disaster Resilience SBA, one of the main activities listed in the GEO Space and Security Community Activity is to get maximum benefit from the use of large and heterogeneous datasets to potentially fill in the observational and capability gaps at EU decision making level.
To this end, the application proposes also the integration of the datasets and tools made available in the frame of the pilot application (weather, citizen science, hydrological and fire models, RASOR platform, Change Detection Maps based on Sentinel-1 and the BEYOND (www.beyond-eocenter.eu) platform – FIREHUB and FloodHub - in synergy with partner NOA and the pilot for resilient ecosystems) for the assessment of impact of natural hazards over areas of interest with regard to human security issues.

Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

title: Assessing Geo-hazard vulnerability of Cities and Critical Infrastructures
full: S6P3 - Assessing Geo-hazard vulnerability of Cities and Critical Infrastructures
org: Instituto Geológico y Minero de España (IGME)
abstract:
Cities account for most of the population in Europe being the engines of the economic growth, but also posing the greatest environmental, social, political and cultural challenges. In order to address them the Urban Agenda for the EU (ratified in May 2016) focuses on priority themes as to improve the quality of life in urban areas; promote the cooperation between cities in the different member states to stimulate growth and innovation; and identify good projects that can be scaled up and transferred across the EU.

Furthermore, the UN SDG Goal 11 “make cities inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable” aims, among others, to significantly reduce the human and economic losses caused by disasters, with a focus on protecting the people in vulnerable situations. In order to develop safer and more secure cities, products and services exploiting Earth Observation technologies can be used to map vulnerable urban areas that could be potentially affected by geo-hazards.

Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.

title: Resilient and Sustainable ecosystems including Agriculture and food
full: S6P4 - Resilient and Sustainable ecosystems including Agriculture and food
abstract:
Natural hazards such as droughts, flash floods, and natural disasters have a dominant role in natural ecosystems, agriculture and hence food, resiliency and sustainability. This pilot is being composed by 3 main pillars: i) Gathering and processing of raw EO and meteo data, integrating with multiple other data sources (in-situ, modeled); ii) Risk disaster modelling derived by NOA (risk assessment on various phenomena droughts, heatwaves, gale winds, hailstorms), atmospheric modelling, flash flooding targeting on timely and accurate information (e.g. warning, alerting), and timely delivery to relevant stakeholders (e.g. farmers, agriculture cooperatives); & iii) Crop type and natural ecosystems mapping leveraging on EO research capacities (TRL 5) relying on machine learning methods in the agriculture domain (e.g. vegetation indices, crop identification etc.), fused with meteo data and coupled with disaster assessments and forecasts, aiming to provide vital thematic information to support the involved user communities (e.g. agriculture agencies, farmers, farming cooperatives) and decision making for the benefit of the agriculture sector and food security. In this pilot, an effective combination of climatological, earth observational, in-situ and state-of-the-art numerical weather prediction data in high resolution is attempted, towards a more sophisticated monitoring of precision agricultural needs.

Acknowledgment
The e-shape project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement 820852.
